whatItIs.text: A hard, granular cow's-milk cheese aged at least 12 months; real Parmigiano Reggiano carries an EU PDO from a defined patch of northern Italy and has been called the king of cheeses.

historyNote.text: The English word 'parmesan' dates to 1519, and since a 2008 EU court ruling, 'Parmesan' in Europe means only Parmigiano Reggiano; outside the EU the name runs free — an Italian farmers' association reported that 90% of 'Italian sounding' cheeses sold in the US are made domestically.

howToChoose.text: Buy wedges, not dust — pre-grated includes anti-caking powder that dulls melt and flavour; PDO-stamped rind means the real thing.

storage.text: Wrap in parchment then a loose layer, and keep in the fridge; hard cheese outlasts soft by months. The rulebook has the details.
storage.note: hard-cheese storage and mould guidance live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: The rind is the best part of the last wedge — it simmers in soups and stocks for umami; hard ends grate into pasta, risotto, and breadcrumbs.

substitutions.note: same family, slightly less crumbly; cheaper
saltier and sharper; reduce added salt
